objectives: Decode taught gr-words by mapping graphemes from left to right.
Blend the gr onset with the vowel and ending to read a complete word.
Distinguish short-vowel words such as grab, grin, and grip.
Reread and self-correct when a consonant or vowel is missed.
concepts: The letters g and r represent two consonants in the initial gr blend.
The vowel and ending must also be decoded.
Short vowels differ and must be heard precisely.
Reading the whole word back checks the sound mapping.

definitions.definition: A letter or group of letters representing a sound.
The consonant sound or blend before the vowel in a syllable.
Noticing an error and repairing it by checking the word again.

workedExamples.solution: Both begin gr and have short /i/, but they end in different sounds.

commonMistakes: Reading only gr and guessing the rest.
Confusing short /a/ in grab with short /i/ in grin.
keyTakeaways: Map every sound from left to right.
revisionPoints: Read the full word to check each sound.

activities.name: Tap, map, blend, and reread gr words.
steps: Listen to or read each target word carefully.
Say or map each sound in the correct order.
Complete the task and explain the sound or text evidence.
Reread or repeat the word to check accuracy.

activities.name: Find and repair a target-pattern error.
steps: Review a word or sentence with one target-pattern error.
Identify the sound, spelling, or evidence that does not match.
Correct the item and explain the correction.
Try a fresh item without looking at the answer.
